edits: The continuation fixes field-update selection boundaries and caption bookmark containment. Update fields/F9 now resolves supported forward cross-references and bookmarked formula dependencies in one pass, with cycle/expansion diagnostics and locked-cache handling. Headless callers opt in with `features.UpdateFields({ ReferenceMode: "Current" })`; the existing snapshot mode remains available. The automation sample includes a formula-linked total and a live IF approval condition comparing native bookmarks. Conditional fields resolve bookmark operands and support omitted false text.

## Conditional bookmark operands

`IF` accepts unquoted bookmark names for either comparison operand. With `ReferenceMode: "Current"`, whole-field bookmark dependencies are resolved before the condition; with `Snapshot`, the original cached bookmark text is compared. Quoted operands remain literal strings. False text may be omitted, producing an empty result when the condition is false.

For example, `IF BudgetAmount >= EstimateTotal "Within budget" "Review estimate"` compares two real bookmarks. The automation sample now bookmarks the displayed DOCVARIABLE budget and calculated total, rather than comparing the budget against a hard-coded initial estimate. Quantity changes followed by F9 update the calculation, linked total and approval together; one undo reverses that field update. Both bookmark operands and the IF instruction survive native DOCX interchange without private metadata.

This implements bookmark operands and optional false text, not nested IF instructions, general inline formula operands, or wildcard matching. Cyclic/unresolved bookmark dependencies retain the condition's cache and report diagnostics; locked dependencies supply their retained values. The comparison target is Microsoft's [IF field contract](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/word/field-codes-if-field); native Word visual/open-save qualification is still separate.

The baseline passed 405 Node tests. The authoring increment plus the continuation adds 105 regressions (510 total) covering formula parsing and bounds, dependency/cycle handling, rich sort identity, header groups, field cache/offset/history fixes, captions/references, Unicode statistics and native DOCX import/export. The continuation adds nine leading-boundary/history regressions and twenty-two dependency/caption/native-DOCX tests, and eight conditional-bookmark/optional-false/native-DOCX tests. Browser coverage is in `word-authoring.browser.mjs`, integrated into the existing full suite; consult the checked commit's CI artifact for the executed result rather than treating test presence as a pass.
